verdict.rationale: Codex documents fine-grained control over external tool access at the session/repo level: engineers can add/remove local or remote MCP servers, inspect available tools before they're used, and set permission boundaries for edits/commands via /permissions (codex-docs-16, codex-docs-38, codex-docs-39, codex-docs-46). This gives an engineer meaningful control over which integrations the agent can reach, and RBAC exists for org/project-level API access (codex-docs-28), but that RBAC is about API/dashboard permissions, not specifically about restricting agent tool/integration access org-wide for a lead managing a team's Codex usage. Missing for 10: evidence of centralized, lead-enforced policy that restricts which MCP servers/tools individual developers can enable (vs. per-session self-configuration), and independent confirmation this control actually prevents unauthorized tool access in practice.
